items.title: Rewiring the ribosome to translate proteins encoded in its own RNA
items.summary: Bacterial ribosomes can synthesize proteins encoded within their own RNA.

items.title: Is this the first glimpse of dark matter? Data point excites physicists
items.summary: An experiment spots an energy flash similar to that of the long-sought weakly interacting massive particle, or WIMP.

items.title: Designing physics experiments with artificial intelligence
items.summary: Artificial intelligence in physics experimental design is explored on the basis of searching for optima over a vast space of hardware configurations and proposing entirely new experimental layouts, rather than tuning a handful of parameters.

items.title: Blood cells replace the immune cells of the ageing human brain
items.summary: At birth, the brain contains its own immune cells, called microglia, that are thought to persist throughout life without being replaced by cells from outside the brain. Studies that trace cell lineage now show that these cells are replaced by circulating immune cells during ageing, revealing a previously unappreciated interaction between the brain and the rest of the body.

items.title: Immune therapy engineered inside the body eases multiple sclerosis
items.summary: Results from a small trial suggest a modified virus can instruct the immune system to wipe out disease-causing cells.

items.title: Connectome analysis of a cerebellum-like circuit for sensory prediction
items.summary: Connectomics, electrophysiology and modelling of electric fish neural circuits shows how distributed synaptic plasticity across multiple network layers cooperates to enable fast, accurate and noise-robust sensory learning.

items.title: Creating bottom-up RNA transfer vehicles from synthetic protein assemblies
items.summary: Synthetic virus-like protein architectures designed by artificial intelligence show superior ability to deliver RNA into cells, compared with their naturally occurring counterparts, by overcoming the evolutionary constraints limiting viral evolution.

items.title: Late-life semaglutide treatment slows ageing and extends lifespan in female mice
items.summary: Semaglutide treatment for 3 months in female mice improved physiological function, attenuated hallmarks of ageing and modulated nutrient sensors and conserved genetic regulators of ageing.

items.title: Weight-loss drug slows ageing in female mice
items.summary: In one inbred strain of laboratory mice, late-life treatment with a GLP-1 drug extends lifespan. This effect might be more than just a consequence of calorie restriction.

items.title: UN finally admits global warming will shoot past 1.5 ºC climate limit
items.summary: Earth will breach a long-standing target before the end of the decade, report says.

items.title: When do infections lead to long COVID? Scientists close in on triggers and treatments for post-viral syndromes
items.summary: Hundreds of millions of people have long-term conditions as a result of an infection. Researchers are working out how to help them.

items.title: Can GLP-1 drugs slow ageing? Mouse study shows promise
items.summary: Older female mice given an anti-obesity medication lived longer and in better health than did mice not taking one.

items.title: Landmark pancreatic cancer drug shows potential against lung cancer too
items.summary: Results bolster hopes that the drug daraxonrasib could prove effective against a variety of tumours.

items.title: Functional chimeric mRNAs encode proteins in mammalian immunity
items.summary: Inflammation induces interchromosomal DNA interactions that bring parent genes into close proximity, facilitating the formation of chimeric mRNAs that encode physiologically relevant, functional proteins.

items.title: 3D epigenome of glial cell types in developing human cortex
items.summary: Integrative 3D epigenomic profiling of four glial cell types from the mid-gestation human cortex reveals cell-type-specific regulatory elements and chromatin interactions that illuminate the roles of non-coding variants in neuropsychiatric disease and human-specific cortical evolution.

items.title: Robust inference and correlates from genetic associations with personality
items.summary: The genetic architecture of personality is robustly generalizable, minimally confounded and widely relevant to human experience.

items.title: Explainable deep learning improves human mental models of self-driving cars
items.summary: Concept-Wrapper Network, a concept-based explanation approach deployed on a real autonomous vehicle, improves drivers’ ability to understand and predict its behaviour.

items.title: Structure and operating principles of a monkeypox virus replisome
items.summary: During replisome assembly of monkeypox virus, the hexameric helicase–primase E5 undergoes large-scale conformational changes that allow two of its primase domains to interact with the polymerase F8 thumb domain and A22 subunit, activating the helicase–primase.

items.title: Anxious or outgoing? Huge study links ‘Big Five’ personality traits to genetic variants
items.summary: Researchers identify more than 1,200 personality-linked genetic variants, with effects largely independent of family background.

items.title: Antimatter ‘tag’ used to detect elusive particle decay
items.summary: A long-underexplored test of particle-physics theory has been revived. This method uses quantum entanglement to infer the presence of undetectable particles.

items.title: NASA’s Roman telescope holds promise far beyond mapping the invisible Universe
items.summary: Discovery flourishes when instruments, ideas and people come together in unpredictable ways.

items.title: Self-driving cars make mistakes, and now users can see why
items.summary: An autonomous-vehicle system that directly explains its decisions in a way that can be interpreted by humans could improve driving safety.

items.title: Audio long read: Could mending damaged DNA prolong life?
items.summary: Researchers are hunting for ways to enhance DNA repair with the hopes that this will keep people healthier for longer.

items.title: Atmospheric CH4 plateau sustained by NOx emission rise and southward shift
items.summary: The atmospheric methane plateau can be explained by tropical hydroxyl radical enhancement primarily driven by a global rise and spatial redistribution of nitrogen oxides emissions towards developing regions and the oceans.

items.title: Intracellular complement factor H protects neurons during CNS inflammation
items.summary: CFH is a key mediator of neuronal resilience across the central nervous system in mice and humans.

items.title: Satellite images before Nepal disaster showed warning signs
items.summary: Images revealed the accelerated movement of a glacier–rock mass just days before it collapsed and triggered a deadly flash flood.

items.title: Peruvian ice has preserved a global methane record
items.summary: The first record of global methane in the tropics, collected from the summit of the mountain Nevado Huascarán in Peru, fills a crucial gap in historical methane data sets. It improves our understanding of the contribution of tropical sources to the past and current global methane distribution.

items.title: Biomarkers that predict improved outcomes after perioperative immune-based therapy for lung cancer
items.summary: Comprehensive exploratory analyses of biomarkers were done in the phase III CheckMate 77T study of pre- and post-surgical treatment with the immunotherapy nivolumab in individuals with surgically resectable non-small-cell lung cancer. The analyses indicate that pre-surgical clearance of circulating tumour DNA, among other markers, is associated with improved clinical outcomes with nivolumab.

items.title: Daily briefing: A thrilling hint of dark-matter discovery
items.summary: A single data point from a dark-matter detector could be the first discovery of the elusive particle. Plus, the grim progress of climate change and whether AI is homogenizing culture and cognition.

items.title: The nutritional value of invertebrate aquatic foods
items.summary: Aquatic invertebrates are exceptionally nutrient dense, supplying the equivalent annual vitamin B12 and selenium requirements for over 5 billion people.

items.title: Aquatic invertebrates contribute substantially to global nutrient supplies
items.summary: An analysis of the nutritional content of aquatic invertebrate species suggests that their global production is a rich source of nutrients that are crucial for human health. The work provides a foundation for better recognition of these valuable invertebrate nutrients and incorporate them into conservation, management and policy efforts.

items.title: Exploring baryon semileptonic decays through polarization and entanglement
items.summary: Polarization and quantum entanglement measurements of baryon semileptonic decay greatly enhance single-event sensitivity, and combined with lattice quantum chromodynamics calculations enable determination of the |Vus| element of the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa matrix, providing an independent test of the standard model.

items.title: Molecular mechanisms and pathogenesis of MASH
items.summary: This Review highlights the state of the art of molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying MASH pathogenesis and its transition to hepatocellular carcinoma.

items.title: Probing far-from-equilibrium dynamics of electrical double layers
items.summary: A new framework combining experimental and computational methods to track ions and water present at an electrode interface allows the molecular structure and evolution of electrical double layers far from equilibrium to be discovered.

items.title: These greenhouse-gas sources have trotters and snouts
items.summary: Emissions linked to global warming are higher at sites where feral pigs disturb the soil.

items.title: When AI does science, who is accountable for mistakes?
items.summary: When AI does science, who is accountable for mistakes?

items.title: Pines grow faster and are more drought resilient in the Southern Hemisphere
items.summary: Non-native conifers from the Northern Hemisphere grow faster and are more drought resistant and resilient in the Southern Hemisphere, where they seem to escape the growth–stress-tolerance trade-off.

items.title: Current therapeutic landscape and future treatment perspectives of MASH
items.summary: The therapeutic landscape and advances in biomarkers for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis are reviewed.

items.summary: Universities and media organizations need to scrutinize their roles in the events that led to this tragedy.
